meta.note: Target-side values for the dimensions added after the freeze of 2026-11-14: wind, dust and ground ice. Never part of the all-round score. A dimension is compared only when the Earth side is published too and a tolerance has been written down.

definitions.wind: Mean wind speed 10 m above the surface, m/s.
definitions.dust: Mean dust or aerosol optical depth of the air column in visible light.
definitions.ice: Share of the ground where water ice is stable at or near the surface, 0 to 1.

wind.source: NASA NSSDCA Moon Fact Sheet: surface pressure about 3 x 10^-15 bar at night
wind.note: The Moon has no atmosphere. There is no wind.

dust.source: NASA NSSDCA Moon Fact Sheet: surface pressure about 3 x 10^-15 bar at night
dust.note: The Moon has no atmosphere. No dust hangs in the air. Lunar dust is a hazard on the ground and on equipment, which an optical depth does not describe.

ice.source: LRO Diviner Polar Resource Product, PDS LRO-L-DLRE-5-PRP-V2.0 (validation/build/moon_temperature.py)
ice.note: Share of the 55.6 km window that never warms above 110 K, where water ice is stable at the surface. Stability, not a detection of ice.

wind.source: Mars Climate Database v6.2 (LMD/OU/IAA/ESA/CNES), climatology scenario (validation/build/mars_environment.py)
wind.note: Mean wind speed 10 m above the surface over the Mars year, from a point query in the model's high-resolution mode. Seasonal means run from 3.14 to 6.96 m/s. A model, not a measurement. The air is about a hundredth as dense as Earth's, so the same speed pushes far less.

dust.source: Mars Climate Database v6.2 (LMD/OU/IAA/ESA/CNES), climatology scenario (validation/build/mars_environment.py)
dust.note: Mean dust optical depth of the whole air column in visible light over the Mars year. Seasonal means run from 0.258 to 0.89. Climate model.

ice.note: No mapped value yet. Shallow ground ice on Mars is mapped by other projects; none is in this data set.
